title: Late Rent Notice | Free Word Template
description: Free late rent notice (pay or quit): amount owed, deadline, late fees and next steps for landlords.
lead: A formal notice from a landlord to a tenant that rent is overdue: how much is owed, by when it must be paid, the late fee and what happens if it is not paid by the deadline.
introParagraphs: A late rent notice (often called a pay-or-quit notice) is the first formal step when a tenant misses rent. It states the amount owed, the deadline to pay, and the next steps (typically eviction) if payment is not received.
Check state and local law for required notice periods, language and delivery method - these vary a lot by jurisdiction and getting it wrong can invalidate an eviction.
bullets: Tenant and property
Tenant name, property address and unit number, landlord/manager contact details.
Amount owed
Total rent past due, the months it covers, any late fee as allowed by the lease or local law, and daily interest if applicable.
Deadline to pay
Number of days to pay or quit (set by state law - often 3, 5, or 14 days) and the exact deadline date.
How to pay
Accepted payment methods and where to send payment.
Consequences
Clear statement that failure to pay by the deadline will result in eviction proceedings as allowed by law.
howTo: Check local law
Confirm the required notice period (pay-or-quit days), content and delivery method for your state/country.
Calculate the amount
Add unpaid rent, any allowed late fees, and any other charges owed under the lease.
Set the deadline
Count the notice days from proper service; state the exact date payment must be received.
Deliver properly
Most jurisdictions require hand delivery, posting on the door plus certified mail. Follow the rules exactly.
Keep proof of service
Have a witness, get a postal receipt, photograph the posted notice, and keep a copy for your file.
related: End-of-tenancy notice (end of lease or cause).
Notice of rent increase before renewal.
If tenant cannot pay in full, set up a written plan.
faq: Do I have to give notice before evicting?
Yes - every state requires some form of pay-or-quit notice before filing eviction. The number of days varies.
Can I change locks or shut off utilities?
No - that is illegal self-help eviction in almost every US state and most countries. You must go through the courts.
Can I accept partial payment?
Yes, but in many jurisdictions accepting partial payment resets the notice period. Put any payment plan in writing.
How do I deliver the notice?
Usually personal service or posting plus certified mail; check local rules. Email alone is rarely enough.
What if they pay after the deadline?
If you accept payment after the deadline you may waive the right to evict for that period; consult local rules.

title: Notice to Vacate | Free Letter Template
description: Free notice to vacate letter from landlord or tenant: end date, move-out terms and inspection.
lead: A formal letter from a landlord ending a tenancy (for cause or end of lease) or from a tenant giving notice they will leave - stating the last day, move-out requirements and next steps.
introParagraphs: A notice to vacate tells the other party the tenancy is ending on a specific date. Landlords use it for non-renewal of a lease, end of a month-to-month tenancy or termination for cause; tenants use it to give required notice before moving out.
Notice periods are set by state and local law (typically 30, 60 or 90 days; longer in rent-controlled areas). Get the period and delivery method right - a defective notice can restart the clock.
bullets: Parties and property
Tenant and landlord/manager names, property address and unit.
Reason (if for cause)
If terminating for cause (non-payment, lease violation), cite the lease clause and any prior notices; no-cause/end-of-lease notices just state the end date.
Move-out date
The date by which the tenant must be out with all belongings and keys returned; calculated from proper service of the notice.
Move-out requirements
Cleaning standard, condition expectations, return of keys, forwarding address for the security deposit.
Next steps
What happens if the tenant does not leave (eviction filing) or what the landlord will do (inspection, deposit return per local law).
howTo: Check required notice period
Confirm the minimum notice days and permitted reasons for your jurisdiction and lease type.
Calculate the vacate date
Count days from proper service (not mailing); state the exact date.
Cite cause if applicable
Reference the lease violation and any prior notices (late rent, unauthorised occupant, etc.).
Deliver as required
Hand delivery, posting plus certified mail, or other method required by local law. Email alone is usually insufficient.
Keep proof of service
Certificate of service signed by the person delivering, plus postal receipts and photographs.
related: Pay-or-quit notice when rent is overdue.
Mutual agreement to end the lease early.
Court-stage notice after notice to vacate expires.
Itemised deductions and refund after move-out.
faq: Landlord or tenant can send it?
Both - landlords serve it to end a tenancy; tenants send it to give required notice they are leaving.
How much notice?
Typically 30-60 days for month-to-month; longer in rent-controlled areas; fixed leases usually expire without notice. Check local law.
Email enough?
Rarely. Most jurisdictions require hand delivery, posting and/or certified mail for termination notices.
What if they don't leave?
You must file eviction (unlawful detainer) in court. Self-help (lockouts, utility shutoffs) is illegal.
Can I revoke the notice?
If the tenant agrees in writing - but if they dispute it you may have to start over.

title: Eviction Notice | Free Letter Template
description: Free eviction notice template: cure-or-quit notice for lease violations leading to eviction proceedings.
lead: A formal notice that eviction proceedings will begin if the tenant does not fix a lease violation (or leave) within the required deadline. Used after pay-or-quit or cure-or-quit deadlines have expired.
introParagraphs: An eviction notice (cure-or-quit or unconditional quit) tells the tenant they have violated the lease and must either fix the violation (cure) or move out (quit) within a set number of days, or the landlord will file for eviction in court.
Eviction is heavily regulated - every step is dictated by state and local law. Using the wrong form, wrong notice period, or wrong delivery method can dismiss your case and force you to start over.
bullets: Tenant and property
Tenant names, property address and unit number, landlord/manager.
Violation
Specific lease violation (non-payment, unauthorised pet, property damage, illegal activity) and dates of prior notices.
Cure or quit
Either fix the violation by X date (pay rent, remove pet, etc.) or vacate the property by Y date.
Unconditional quit
For severe violations (illegal activity, repeated non-payment, substantial damage), the notice may require leaving without option to cure.
Court filing warning
Notice that failure to comply will result in an unlawful detainer/eviction lawsuit and possible money judgment.
howTo: Get legal guidance
Consult a landlord-tenant attorney or local housing authority on the correct notice type and period.
Use the correct form
Cure-or-quit for curable violations; unconditional quit for severe breaches; pay-or-stay/quit for rent only.
Reference prior notices
Cite dates and types of any earlier notices already served on the tenant.
Deliver per statute
Follow exact service rules - hand it to the tenant, post on the door AND mail certified, as required.
File with the court if needed
If the tenant does not comply by the deadline, file for eviction in the appropriate court with proof of service.
related: Mutual early move-out instead of eviction.
Formal demand for unpaid rent before court.
faq: Can I evict without notice?
Almost never. Even illegal activity usually requires some notice. Self-help eviction (lockouts, shutting off utilities) is illegal everywhere.
How long is the notice?
3-30 days depending on state, reason and lease type. Illegal activity can sometimes be 24 hours; non-payment typically 3-14 days.
Do I need a lawyer?
Small claims/landlord-tenant court may allow self-representation but an attorney is recommended for anything complex.
What if they pay during the notice?
In most states full payment of rent within the pay-or-quit period stops the eviction for that non-payment episode.
How long does eviction take?
Anywhere from 2 weeks to 3+ months depending on the state, court backlog and tenant defences.

title: Sublease Agreement | Free Word Template
description: Free sublease agreement template: subtenant, rent, term, rules and landlord consent for subletting.
lead: A contract between a tenant (sublessor) and a subtenant who rents part or all of the rental from them, with the original landlord's written consent - setting out rent, dates, rules and responsibilities.
introParagraphs: A sublease lets an existing tenant rent out all or part of their unit to someone else while remaining responsible to the landlord for the original lease terms. The original tenant becomes a landlord to the subtenant.

Always get the landlord's written consent before subletting - subletting without consent usually violates the lease and can be grounds for eviction. Check local law too; some cities restrict the landlord's ability to refuse.
bullets: Parties and landlord consent
Original tenant (sublessor), subtenant, landlord consent (written approval attached), property address and unit.
Term and access
Start and end date (must not exceed original lease), what part the subtenant occupies (private room, whole unit), and how and when the sublessor can enter.
Rent and bills
Monthly rent amount, due date, payment method, security deposit (within legal caps), and split of utilities, internet and other bills.
Rules and responsibilities
House rules (quiet hours, guests, smoking, pets), who handles maintenance, and obligations to follow the master lease.
Default and termination
What happens if the subtenant misses rent, notice required to end the sublease, and that the subtenant agrees the master lease rules apply.
howTo: Get landlord consent first
Ask in writing; attach the proposed sublease and subtenant information (income, references).
Screen the subtenant
Run a credit check, references and verify income - you remain liable for rent and damage.
Set rent and deposits
Rent can be up to what you pay (or more in some markets); security deposit limits usually mirror local landlord-tenant law.
Define the space
State which room/area is the subtenant's and what is shared (kitchen, bathroom, common areas).
Sign and move in
Both sign, attach the landlord consent and master lease, collect the deposit and first month's rent, and do a move-in walk-through.
related: The master lease the subtenant must also follow.
For roommates on the same lease (not subletting).
For renting a room within an occupied home.
Screen the subtenant like any tenant.
How to write a sublease agreement
faq: Do I need landlord permission?
Almost always yes. Subletting without consent is usually a lease violation that can get you evicted. Some cities/campuses require 'good cause' for the landlord to refuse.
Am I still liable?
Yes - you are still the tenant on the master lease and owe rent even if the subtenant stops paying you. The landlord will come after you, not the subtenant.
Can I charge more rent?
Sometimes yes; some rent-control areas cap sublet rent. Check local rules.
Who does the subtenant pay?
Usually you, and you continue paying the landlord. Or the subtenant can pay the landlord directly, but you remain responsible.
Can I evict the subtenant?
Yes - you act as their landlord and must follow the same eviction process (notice, court) required in your jurisdiction.

title: Roommate Agreement | Free Word Template
description: Free roommate agreement: rent split, chores, guests, quiet hours, bills and moving out terms.
lead: A written agreement between roommates covering rent split, bills, chores, guests, quiet hours, food, security deposits and how to handle someone moving out early.
introParagraphs: A roommate agreement sets expectations between people sharing a rental so small disagreements do not turn into disputes. It covers how rent and bills are split, chores, guests, quiet hours, and what happens if one roommate leaves early.

It does not replace the lease with the landlord - all roommates on the lease are jointly and severally liable for full rent to the landlord. The roommate agreement governs how roommates split costs and rules between themselves.
bullets: Rent and deposit
Each roommate's share of rent and the security deposit, due date, and who pays the landlord.
Bills and utilities
How rent, electricity, gas, water, internet and streaming services are split and whose name they are in.
Chores and common areas
Cleaning schedule, shared groceries, who takes out bins, dish/kitchen rules, smoking/vaping and pets.
Guests and quiet hours
How often guests can stay over, overnight guest rules, parties, noise/quiet hours aligned with the lease.
Moving out early
Notice period required if a roommate leaves, how a replacement is found, and whether the departing roommate still owes rent.
howTo: Talk it through first
Sit down together and discuss rent, bills, cleaning, guests and food before drafting.
Split rent fairly
Equal split is normal; unequal room size may justify different amounts. Be clear who pays the landlord each month.
Set guest and noise rules
Decide on overnight guests, parties and quiet hours - make them compatible with the lease.
Decide food and chores
Shared vs separate food, a cleaning rota or expectations, and who buys shared supplies.
Sign and each keep a copy
All roommates sign; attach a copy to the lease if the landlord wants one.
related: When someone replaces a roommate via sublet.
The master lease with the landlord.
For a landlord renting a room to a tenant.
What to include in a roommate agreement
faq: Is a roommate agreement legally binding?
Yes - as between roommates, a signed agreement is a contract a court can enforce for rent contributions and shared costs.
Does it bind the landlord?
No - the lease is between tenants and landlord. The landlord is not a party to the roommate agreement.
If my roommate leaves early, am I stuck with full rent?
To the landlord - yes, all lease signers are jointly liable. The roommate agreement lets you sue your ex-roommate for their share.
Can I evict a roommate?
If they are on the lease, generally no - the landlord must do it. If they are your subtenant, you can as their landlord (see sublease).
How do we split the security deposit?
Proportional to what each paid; document condition at move-in so damages can be fairly assigned.
